MAST parameters

Source: R/tool-mast.R
mastParam.Rd

Parameters for GiottoClass::analyzeData() that run MAST (Finak et al. 2015), which tests each feature for differential expression between two groups of cells with a hurdle model: a logistic regression for whether the feature is detected and a linear regression for its level where it is. The likelihood ratio test combines both parts. MAST is a Bioconductor package, install it with BiocManager::install("MAST"). If you use it, please cite the original paper (see References).

Usage

mastParam(
  method = c("bayesglm", "glm", "ridge", "blmer", "glmer"),
  ebayes = TRUE
)

# S4 method for class 'allMatrix,mastParam'
analyzeData(
  x,
  param,
  groups,
  test,
  ref,
  covariates = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

method

fitting method passed to MAST::zlm(): "bayesglm" (MAST's default), "glm", "ridge", "blmer" or "glmer"

ebayes

logical, shrink the variances with empirical Bayes (MAST's default TRUE)

x

expression matrix, features x cells (MAST expects log-scale values; it is made dense)

param

a mastParam

groups

group label of each cell. Named by cell ID (matched to colnames(x)) or in the column order of x. Cells labelled NA are left out.

test, ref

the labels in groups to compare: test against ref

covariates

NULL or a data.frame with one row per column of x and the covariates to adjust for (e.g. the detection rate)

verbose

show MAST's progress messages

Value

A mastParam object.

Details

analyzeData(x, param, groups, test, ref, covariates) returns a data.table with one row per feature, sorted by fdr: feats, Pr(>Chisq) (the hurdle likelihood ratio test), coef, ci.hi and ci.lo (the log fold change of test over ref and its confidence interval), fdr (Benjamini-Hochberg) and cluster ("<test>_vs_<ref>").

References

Finak G, McDavid A, Yajima M, Deng J, Gersuk V, Shalek AK, Slichter CK, Miller HW, McElrath MJ, Prlic M, Linsley PS, Gottardo R. MAST: a flexible statistical framework for assessing transcriptional changes and characterizing heterogeneity in single-cell RNA sequencing data. Genome Biology 16, 278 (2015). doi:10.1186/s13059-015-0844-5

See also

runMAST()

Examples

p <- mastParam(method = "glm")
p$method
